done.why: I had seen the main changes, died once to a grue and was dumped in the forest, and stopped there.

about: A remixed Zork I. The house is familiar, but the cellar's south exit now leads to a chasm edge, then a gallery and a studio with a painting. A chimney has a strict carry limit. The troll waits north of the cellar.

moments.note: South from the cellar reached a chasm edge, a gallery and a studio, not the classic layout.
The chimney refuses to carry more than the lamp and one item, and going back down it is refused. I had to walk around.
The troll eats the lantern when given it. I had no light afterwards.
Walking in the dark killed me to a grue straight away.

wished: To go back down the chimney.
To see what the troll does if fought with the sword.

lines.line: You can't get up there with what you're carrying... The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It states the new rule clearly.

lines.line: The troll, who is not overly proud, graciously accepts the gift and not having the most discriminating tastes, gleefully eats it.
lines.why: It rewards a contrary move with humor.

fun.why: Familiar space with surprises, and playing against the rules got funny answers.

engagement.why: I stopped early, but the new rooms pulled me along.

difficulty.why: The carry limit and the dark were fair but unforgiving.

interestingness.why: The altered geography and the chimney rule gave me new things to learn.

prose.why: It is crisp, with classic Zork wit.
